newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Vance panel to explore fate of missing Bosnians.
newsitem.headline: Vance panel to explore fate of missing Bosnians.

text.p: An international commission, which ended its first meeting on Friday, said it would try to speed investigations into the fate of 14,000 Bosnians missing in the 43-month-long war.
The pressure group, announced by U.S. President Clinton last June, is headed by former U.S. Secretary of State Cyrus Vance, previously a mediator of the Bosnian peace talks.

The International Commission on Missing Persons in the former Yugoslavia agreed to set up a survivors fund, open an office in Sarajevo and seek mine clearance to faciliate exhumation of mass graves, according to a final statement issued by the U.S. diplomatic mission.
"The purpose of the session was tf the missing-person effort and to permit them to identify important areas for attention," it said.

Members expressed support for a working group, established under the Dayton Peace Accords last December and chaired by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), which is trying to trace those unaccounted for. An ICRC official this week put the number at 14,000, including Moslems, Serbs and Croats.
Regarding mass graves, the statement said the Commission would seek to "obtain priority for mine clearance and security activity associated with humanitarian exhumations".
Michael Steiner, deputy civilian high representative for former Yugoslavia who attended the two-day talks as an adviser, told a news conference:

"The fact is that there are some 10,000 families who are missing their brothers, sons and husbands. They think their family members are still alive, although objectively one must assume that most are dead."

"The Commission will make clear to authorities on the ground that they have to cooperate in the process of identifying missing persons, opening up mass graves and clearing the sites of mortal remains. It is he parties) have to do it. It will take many years because there are so many mass graves and unidentified persons."

The other six members are: former British Foreign Secretary Lord Carrington, ICRC President Cornelio Sommaruga, Max van der Stoel, high commissioner on national minorities for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), former French Justice Minister Robert Badinter, former Pakistani Foreign Minister Sahabzada Yaqub-Khan, and U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights Jose Ayala-Lasso.
